title: Jeanne d'Arc
subtitle: A familiar history becomes a fantasy

body: Jeanne d'Arc is Level-5's tactical role-playing game for PSP, first released in Japan on 22 November 2006. Its Joan of Arc inhabits a fantasy version of the Hundred Years' War, where magical powers and monsters accompany the struggle against English forces. Jeanne gathers companions and leads them across a succession of battlefields. The historical outline supplies names and a direction for the journey, while the supernatural elements give its combat another set of possibilities. Animated sequences and expressive characters introduce a campaign designed around battles fought one decision at a time.

Battles take place on a grid, with each member of the party moving and acting in turn. Weapon reach, surrounding allies and the direction of an approach affect what can be achieved from one square. Special skills offer attacks and recovery beyond the basic options, giving each character another role to develop. The player must consider the group rather than only Jeanne: leaving one fighter isolated can make the next enemy turn dangerous, while a careful formation creates opportunities for several companions to support the same advance.

Magical armlets allow certain characters to transform, temporarily gaining strength and additional abilities. Choosing when to use that advantage becomes part of managing a difficult encounter. Skill gems can be equipped and combined, letting the party's development continue between battles. Ken Motomura directed Level-5's first tactical role-playing game and its first PSP production, with Takeshi Inoue composing the music. The original release reached North America in 2007. Its later PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 edition in 2024 also brought the adventure to European audiences for the first time.
